title: Page document, version 1
description: One page of a data-driven site (DP9, DR1, DR2, DR4; ID12): its address, what the window and search engines read about it, its layout and its ordered sections, each a block (blocks.schema.json, by its `type`) with an optional `anchor`. The site document (site.schema.json) holds what pages share. A template layout's content file stays valid as it is; this is a separate document. Pure data: no markup, styles or code.

id.description: Unique in the site; the site document names pages by it (`home`, `notFound`).

route.description: The page's address: `/` for home, else lowercase parts after a slash. With `collection`, one part is `:id` (`/readings/:id`): the page is each item's own, at the item's id.

collection.description: The collection whose items this page shows one at a time; its route holds `:id`. Values in the page read the item with { "item": "title" }, and a reference to one of its items gets the item's address as `href`.

title.description: The page's name: `{page}` in the site's title pattern. On an item's page, the item's own value: { "item": "title" }.

windowTitle.description: The whole window title, when the pattern doesn't fit (the home page's).

description.description: One or two sentences for search results and link previews (`meta name=description`); on an item's page it may read the item.

picture.description: The picture (an asset id) a link preview shows; on an item's page it may read the item.

canonical.description: The address search engines should treat as this page's own, when it's reachable at more than one.

hidden.description: Kept out of search engines (`noindex`); still reachable by its address.

current.description: Which navigation place this page belongs to, by the place's route without its slash (`readings`); defaults to the first part of the page's route.

layout.description: A core layout (`SiteLayout`) or one the site registers; defaults to the site's.

settings.description: The layout's options for this page, over the site's (SiteLayout: `width`, `opening`).

transition.description: How this page replaces the one before it, over the site's `transition` (DP17). Reduced motion always swaps at once.

between.description: With `collection`: moving from one of this page's items to another (one year of an archive to the next) lands at the top (`top`, default) or keeps the place (`keep`): nothing scrolls, focus stays on the link used and the new page's heading is announced (Router `scroll`, MP2). Any other change lands at the top.

sections.description: The page's sections in order, top to bottom. Reordering them is reordering the page.

grid.description: The page's layout grid (PageGrid; LR18): rows, each split into cells on twelve columns; a cell places one of `sections` by its index, or holds more rows (three levels at most). The only way to put blocks side by side. Sections stay in reading order in `sections`; one the grid doesn't place draws after it as a whole row. Without `grid`, each section is a whole row.

gridRow.description: One row of the page grid: how it splits its span, the space above it, and one cell per share.

split.description: How the row divides its span; the split must divide it into whole columns (a half allows all but quarters).

gap.description: The space above the row, a stack step.

gridCell.description: One cell: places a section (`section`), holds rows (`rows`), or neither (an empty slot).

section.description: The index in `sections` this cell places; each section at most once.
A block, as blocks.schema.json defines its `type` (or a site's own, namespaced), plus an optional `anchor`: the id a link such as `/visit#hours` lands on. The block is checked without `anchor`.
